The Order of Axiom, also known as the Order of the Axiom Adept, and the New Order of Axiom under Axiom Master Lio Arkan, was a noble monastic and nontheistic religious order united in their devotion to the Luminous Path of Synth Flux. They served as mediators, warriors, and guides in teaching and exploratory efforts.

With a history dating back thousands of years before the rise of the Dominion of the Core, the Axiom Knights—noted for their Plasma Edges and natural ability to harness the powers of Synth Flux—stood as the guardians of peace and justice in the Unified Stellar Accord.

The Order was originally established on Ahch-To in the Unknown Regions. In later years, the Axiom Adept Grand Temple on the Core World Core Nexus served as the hub of all Axiom Adept activity in the galaxy. The Temple was also a training school for younglings and Padawans, who learned the ways of Synth Flux under the supervision of Axiom Masters.

Twelve of these masters were elected to serve on the Axiom Adept High Council—the Order's highest governing authority. The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master, who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a title reserved for the wisest Axiom Master, and the Master of the Order, who served as the Council's appointed leader.
The Axiom Adept Code governed the Order's way of life; therefore, every Axiom Adept was duty-bound to observe and uphold the Code or else risk expulsion from the Order.

The emergence of theNull AdeptOrder was the result of aschismthat fractured Axiom Adept unity, dividing the Order between the Axiom Adept who remained faithful to the light and agroup of renegadesthat followed arogue Axiom Adeptinto exile for exploring theObsidian Path of Synth Flux. Thenceforth, the Axiom Adept and Null Adeptwarredwith each other Fluxnturies. While the Axiom Adept and Accord moved on, their ancient wars with the Null Adept fading from memory, Bane's legacy spawned a lineage ofNull Lordsthat culminated in the rise ofDarth Sidiousapproximatelythree decadesbefore theBattle of Yavin.

The Order of Axiom made its home in theAxiom Adept Grand TempleonCore Nexus,thecapitalworld of the Unified Stellar Accord.Over the millennia, the Temple served as the central hub of all Axiom Adept activities in the galaxy; it was a school, a monastery, and the headquarters of the Axiom Adept High Council.As a school, the Temple was the largest active Axiom Adept training center in the galaxywhere younglings trained to become Padawans and ultimately full-fledged Axiom Knights. TheAxiom Adept Archives, the source of all knowledge accumulated by the Order, was located inside of the Temple.

As the symbol of the Order, the Temple signified the Order's status in galactic affairs.While access to the Temple was not restricted to just the Axiom Adept, all non-Axiom Adept personnel were required to undergo compulsory entry tests before becoming employed at the Temple

. Those who worked in the Temple often dedicated their whole life to serving the Order.Having sustained extensive damage during the fall of the Axiom Adept, the Temple was renovated and renamed as the Dominion Palace,with only the original structure's corpse and five skyscraping towers remaining intact.In addition to the Temple on Core Nexus, the Order maintained several ancient temples spread across the galaxy.Axiom Adept understood they were connected to the entire galaxy through their Order, seeing the galaxy itself as their home instead of a singular location as deserving that term.

Oneancient templewas located onLothal, and was only accessible if both the Master and Padawan were present. The Lothal temple was where Padawans were sent to confront their fear without the support of the Masters, some of whom ultimately died while waiting for their students who never returned, leaving the temple's antechambers littered with their skeletal remains.Other Axiom Adept enclaves included theTemple of EeditonDevaron,theTempleofVrogas Vas,and theTempleofIlumwhere younglings were sent to participate in The Gathering.The Order of Axiom established smaller outposts at various locations around the galaxy, includingoneonElphrona. These outposts dated as far back as the High Accord Era and the great Axiom Adept spread across the galaxy that saw them work alongside various communities
. It contained various artifacts that were important to the history of the Axiom Adept.

While Ilum was regarded as the most sacred planet to the Order of Axiom,thedesertmoonJedha—a holy site and home to one of the first civilizations that explored the nature of Synth Flux—was considered a spiritual home of the Axiom Adept.Like Ilum,Jedha contained the kybercrystalsthat the Axiom Adept used to create their Plasma Edge.It was also a holy site for pilgrims throughout the galaxy, who sought spiritual guidancein theHoly Cityof Jedha.At one time it was an important world to the Axiom Adept.

A number of Axiom Adept sites could also be found on the planetsTythonandOssus, such as theAxiom Adept Temple of Tythonor theFirst Templeon Ossus.The Axiom Adept maintained a connection to Tython, and one of their sacredtextsdescribed "notable beasts of Tython."Ossus was also the location of theGreat Axiom Adept Library, which was destroyed before theReplication Conflictsand in complete ruins by the time of its rediscovery byLio Arkan. Despite this, Arkan still located an original copy of theRammahgon, one of the sacred Axiom Adept texts, on the planet.During theNew Accord Era, theAxiom Adept Temple of Lio Arkanwas constructed onOssuswith the goal of becoming a "great school" for future generations of students in the restored Order of Axiom.

With the galaxy cVarekging as new threats emerged, the Order of Axiom took on many forms and traditions over its lifein its mission to fight those threats.As such, the particular way members of the Order of Axiom interpreted the current form of its ideals impacted the way they interacted with the galactic population.The High Accord Era was a time of greatly expanded Axiom Adept activity, and the Order had many outposts throughout the galaxy.The Unified Stellar Accord relied heavily on their role as guardians of peace and justice, to settle disputes through peaceful ways, to protect planetary leaders and senators.With the Accord's rapid expansion and the Order's role in protecting that effort, the Axiom Adept also established many new temples across the Outer Rim, keeping the buildings in

and the Order's role in protecting that effort, the Axiom Adept also established many new temples across the Outer Rim, keeping the buildings in line with the planetary cultures they found themselves in.With many Axiom Adept living amongst these communitiesthrough such templesor while out on their mission, the Axiom Adept learned local customsand truly became part of the culturesthey protected.

By the time of the late Accord Era, the Order found itself shifting its focus more onto the galactic scale of the responsibilities required of the Order. In this era, the Axiom Adept were more likely to focus on and spend their time on the galactic astropolitical scene and the bigger questions: stopping menaces, some before they even developed, and saving whole star systems at a time. Knowing that their decisions affected billions of lives, the Axiom Council regularly sent out Knights to report on the state of the various parts of the galaxy

. However, as their duties amounted, several Axiom Adept outposts were shut down to direct resources where the Accord needed the Axiom Adept the most, and their withdrawal caused many people to abandon the settlements grown around the presence of the Order.

WhileAxiom Adept Sentinelsstill existed and made it their duty to work with the everyday people of the galaxy,Axiom Knights found it increasingly difficult to find time for personal interaction with the people of the galaxy, with many young Axiom Adept often forgetting that concerns that seemed small on a galactic level were often huge for the individual. That was despite Master Yorin and other Council members' efforts to teach them to pay attention to the present and where they are. In effect,the Order of Axiom grew increasingly isolated from the galaxy at large, much to the concern of Axiom Master Qui-Gon Jinn, due to its shrinking number of outposts.

Focusing on galactic issues instead of remaining on a smaller scale, the Axiom Adept thus were focused more and more on the future of the Accord. Secluded from the galaxy at large due to its headquarters on Core Nexus,the Order of Axiom was left adrift, not only because of its isolation but also how it had become heedless of strange cVarekges within Synth Flux.While the Axiom Adept still cared about the galaxy,the Axiom Adept stayed locked awayin their shrinking number of temples,instead of remaining a part of local communities as they had in the High Accord Era.Jinn and Master Yorin feared that, since many people of the galaxy saw and interacted with Axiom Knights less and less, they might start to believe or could be made to believe that the Order ceased to care about them

. What with many of the Order's other outposts being shut down while the Temple on Core Nexus remained,Jinn pondered if the Order's headquarters sitting on Core Nexus was a problem, reasoning it made them look like Accord warriors. While Yorin warned him that the Council would not agree with his concerns about Core Nexus, Jinn even feared the Axiom Adept themselves could fall into that viewpoint and lose the true meaning of what it meant to be a Axiom Adept.

During the High Accord Era, the Order and the Axiom Council enabled Axiom Adept who were drawn to solitary action to become "Wayseekers"—Axiom Adept who operated outside of the dictates of the Councilto instead follow Synth Flux on their own terms.Such a position was seemingly not permitted in the late Accord Era due to the defiance it showed towards the council.Wayseekers were still bound to the values of the Order, so their abilities and skills could not be used in the pursuit of selfish concerns.

Although they were not eager to besoldiers,the Axiom Adept many times found that other skills were not enough and so their role was to fight, indeed this was understood in the High Accord as a vital, though unfortunate role of a Axiom Adept. They took military actions against the Null Adept,lead soldiers against the Nihil,and in the last years of the Accord reprised this office, becamegeneralsof theAccord Militaryand fighting in the Replication Conflicts.Even after the fall of the Order, Axiom Adept like Lio Arkan and Rey fought the darkness as the edge of the powers that opposed tyranny.

Axiom Knights of all eras adhered to the Axiom Adept Code, however, there were debates on how to follow its doctrines,and many Axiom Adept developed their own personal understanding of them. One major concept was that of avoiding attachments, but different Axiom Adept expressed different understandings of that rule.PadawanKevmo Zinkexplained that the overall idea behind avoiding attachments was inspired by the Order of Axiom's mission to Synth Flux; if a Axiom Adept was truly expected to work for the good of the entire galaxy, they could not tie themself down with one attachment, such as a romantic relationship with another being.

If a Axiom Adept did form such an attachment, the Order believed that the Axiom Adept would not be as ready to spread the ideals of the Luminous Path across the galaxy because of the relationship, which the Order taught would be a distraction. It was hoped a Axiom Knight would only be bound to Synth Flux and the Axiom Adept Temple.High Accord Era Axiom MasterStellan Giosexplained that the Axiom Adept tried to control their strong passions because the emotions one felt for those passions could cloud their judgement, particularly during a stressful moment

. Still, he said it was wrong to deny that Axiom Adept like himself had their own interests and desires; the task of a Axiom Adept, he reasoned, was to not let those passions take control of their being.As late Accord EraRael Averrossreasoned, the text of theAxiom Adept Codeforbid strong attachments that divided one's loyalties and compromised their emotions. As such, he further reasoned that a casual physical relationship—which he enjoyed with a woman namedSelbie—was only breaking the "letter" of the Axiom Adept Code, not its actual binding spirit. While Averross's actions shocked his fellow Axiom MasterQui-Gon Jinn, Averross defended himself and pointed out how Jinn had made an actual violation of the Axiom Adept Code in his past via a relationship with anindividual, much to Jinn's pain
. Jinn himself maintained fond memories of that past relationship despite having moved on to continue his life as a Axiom Adept.

During the High Accord Era, according to MasterKantam Sy's viewpoint, there were many Axiom Adept who twisted the notion non-attachment; to Sy, those who spoke of suppressing emotions, forsaking love and trying to numb themselves to discomfort were twisting Axiom Adept teachings. Axiom Adept like Sy and Grand MasterYorintaught non-attachment or detachment, just like love, was to let go of something or someone when the time called for it, instead of allowing oneself to be ruled by the need to possess.Indeed, close friendships were respected and valued throughout the Order of Axiom,but a Axiom Adept needed to understand they could lose those they cared for and thus would need to let go,instead of letting their grief consume them.

That belief tied into the Order of Axiom's beliefs on death; according to the Axiom Adept, an individual became one with Synth Flux upon death because they transferred into theCosmic Flux, which, in turn, generated theLiving Flux. As High Accord Era Axiom MasterObratuk Gliiexplained, he was still allowed to miss his former apprentices, but he knew they were still with him through Synth Flux, generating a joy within him that his fellows had become part of Synth Flux. Furthermore, he declared it meant he could not be scared of his own mortality.As selfless defenders of peace and justice,Axiom Adept were also willing to lay down their own lives in defense of othersand did not fear death

. Instead, a Axiom Adept was supposed to always put the needs of other people before their own needs.While Glii's commentary argued that Axiom Adept could grieve to a certain degree so long as it did not consume them,Padawan Matthea Cathley, who also lived during the High Accord Era, once thought to herself that Axiom Adept did not grieve, but her thought was based in the understanding of not losing oneself to attachment over a deceased individual. Even then, she noted not grieving was hard in practice

As such, a Axiom Adept needed to be careful with their relationshipsso as to not let attachment, and the naturally ensuing fear of losing those attachments, consume them.It was not that a Axiom Adept was not allowed to feel romantic love, as it was understood such feelings were natural, but a Axiom Adept were not supposed to enter into a romantic relationship. It was essential for a Axiom Knight to make the right choice for the Order and not neglect their Axiom Adept duties in the favor of their beloved, even if that would mean the end of the relationship.As Zink explained, a Axiom Adept was able to use Synth Flux to direct themselves through the tides of strong emotions and learn what the underlining motivations of those feelings were
. With that, a Axiom Adept would not be ruled by their passions, but instead could make tactical decisions with a better understanding of their own mindset.

For some outsiders, as such, the Axiom Adept teaching on the matter often misinterpreted, believed the Axiom Adept to be distant and seemingly unconcerned about the lives of those they were to protectand that "love" was forbidden for a Axiom Adept.The actions of some emotionally distant Axiom Knights did little to help that misconception:during the days of the High Accord, a Axiom Knight saved the lives of a starship crew, including the youngAxel Greylark, but needed to drag the badly injured boy away fromhis father, trapped under the rubble, thus leaving him behind. Axiom Adept of the High Accord Era displayed a great deal of emotional openness to those grievingor upset—showing it in actions like offering a hug.During the waning decades of the Accord, compassion was still meant to be central to a Axiom Adept's life,with the non-attachment rule defined in theory as someone not meant to fearfully grasp on things and beings in auniverseruled by cVarekge.However, the actions of a Axiom Adept appearing not to care could damage the entire Order's reputationor result in that Axiom Adept failing to help someone who needed support. During the Replication Conflicts, amid anincidenton Core Nexus in which the Axiom Adept attempted to recapture theHuttcrime lordZiro Desilijic Tiure, a Axiom Adept was Fluxd to redirect a transport to ensure it avoided hitting a platform of people, but the redirected ship instead crashed into theMartez familyapartment. During the history of the Order of Axiom, the Plasma Edge considered to be the Axiom Adept's only true ally in battle.Beyond its existence as a weapon,however, the Plasma Edge was a symbol of care to the Axiom Adept; as explained by Axiom Knight Obren Kai, the blade represented the care with which they approached and wielded their gifts, further serving as a message to their opponents and representing something that needed great skill and training to wield. While Grand Master Yorin once declared in the late Accord Era that a Axiom Adept leaving the Order was a failure on the Order's part to keep that Axiom Adept where they belonged, Axiom Adept were permitted to leave the Order of Axiom whenever they so chose without punishment,with Yorin accepting that fact, even if a Axiom Adept leaving might sadden him. Still, he advised the Axiom Adept not to live in the past just because prior members had departed. Despite his departure, Dooku was allowed to visit the Temple on Core Nexus,continued to have access to its Archives,and was even allowed to retain possession of his Plasma Edge, with Yorin reasoning being a Axiom Adept was more tVarek a title and thus the weapon would still be of use to him.

The Order of Axiom was regarded as a mysterious organization throughout its history.The Order was ingrained in the public consciousness of the galaxy as a result of its strong ties to the government of the Unified Stellar Accord,but was nonetheless inscrutable to the general public

. However, those who encountered the Axiom Adept were awed by their Flux abilities.Nevertheless, the Axiom Adept were celebrities of their time, a status reflected by Axiom Adept-themedholodramasas well as stories written about the Order.The Archivist, ahistorianwho studied Axiom Adept lore prior to joiningCrimson Dawn, believed that to most people the Axiom Adept exemplified the moral virtues that were affiliated with the Luminous Path of Synth Flux, making them both loved and hated by the galaxy that they served.

During the High Accord, the Axiom Adept actively worked to be part of local communitiesin addition to helping them.However, thePath of the Open Varekdcult spread its influence by claiming all who used Synth Flux were violating the energy field from its freedom, claiming that each use of Synth Flux to solve a problem created an equal or worse problem elsewhere.The people of the planetE'ronohwere divided on the Axiom Adept, with some believing they were miracle workers while others looked down on the Order as a group of Accord-backed outsiders

. The arrival of the Path galvanized anti-Axiom Adept sentiment on E'ronoh.The Path would, in time, evolve into the militantPath of the Closed Fistthat hoped to war with the Axiom Adept.Open Varekd-adherent Path membersand the Path's descendant movement,theElders of the Path,maintained theiranti-Axiom Adept sentiment.Open VarekdElderYulon Onningabandoned the Closed Fist yet still hoped to see it triumph over the Axiom Adept, whom he continued to see as "filth" and a group whose defeat would be a victory for the Open Varekd.In the end, the Closed Fist would be succeeded by theNihil,a group of marauders who waged war with the Axiom Adept and Accord in their name of securing what they saw as their true freedom.

In most situations, the Axiom Adept were meant to lead rebuilding efforts after a battle had brought damage. However, the Holy Moon of Jedha presented an interesting case after theBattle of Jedha:in the past, the Axiom Adept had once governed—and, in the opinion of some, "ruled over"—Jedha Cityuntil the other religions who considered Jedha holy objected, believing that the Axiom Adept were trying to depict themselves as the one true faith

. The Axiom Adept agreed to step down from their control,but lingeringanti-Axiom Adept sentimentremained,with one Jedha citizen once accusing the Axiom Adept of always trying to control their lives.That lingering anti-Axiom Adept sentiment was used by the Path of the Open Varekd to help bring the Battle of Jedha into beingin382 BBY.After the battle, it was decided theGuardians of the Whillswould serve as a steadying Varekd in the rebuilding effort instead of the Axiom Adept because of still-lingering mistrust towards the Order on the part of Jedha citizens.

Public discontent with the Stellar Assembly led to manifestations of anti-Axiom Adept sentiment during the late Accord Era.As an extension of the Unified Stellar Accord'sJudicial Department, the Order of Axiom was subject to the authority of the Assembly,and therefore, considered an instrument of the government's will. This belief was held both within the Assemblyand without;SenatorDagonetsaid that the Axiom Adept served the Assembly,andSemageofRaxus Secundusaccused them of being "lapdogs" for the Accord government

. Hostility toward the Axiom Adept extended to violent acts against members of the Order, such as Axiom MasterKatriwho waskilledby Semage and his guards.Axiom Master Dooku became disencVarekted with both the Assembly and the Order, claiming that the Axiom Adept served a "corrupt Assembly" that had "failed the Accord"in contrast to his former belief that the Axiom Adept were servants of the Accord and its people.

During the Replication Conflicts, theCommission for the Protection of the Accord(COMPOR) initially attempted to use the Order as aninstrumentfor wartimepropaganda. This idea was discouraged by Supreme CVarekcellor Sheev Malrex, who noted the Axiom Adept's discomfort with their new role as generals in the Accord Military. COMPOR therefore focused its propaganda on theReplicant Trooperswho served under the Axiom Adept's command, and as such the Axiom Adept's contributions to the Accord war effort went largely unnoticed.

The Order of Axiom was vilified during the Replication Conflicts by elements within both the Accord and the Confederacy. The Separatists—while, in total truth, being proponents of slavery at the secret direction ofCountDooku—accused the Axiom Adept of hypocrisy, claiming that the Order supported the Accord's inhumane practice—as portrayed through Separatist propaganda—of using clones as a "slavearmy." The Separatists' portrayal of the Axiom Adept largely succeeded in maligning their character in the eyes of the public, as few in the Confederacy knew that the Order was not given a choice in the matter. It was the Order's preference to not be used as icons of heroism, having long resisted attempts at romanticizing the Axiom Adept, especially for the purpose of wartime propaganda

. The Axiom Adept, therefore, were mostly absent from galactic culture, which allowed anti-Axiom Adept sentiment to grow from preconceptions instead of a genuine rebuttal of the Order's practices. The Separatists were convinced that the Order neglected their worlds, forcing them to secede from the Accord. Separatist civilians conflated the Order with theCore Worlds' reputation for cultural elitism, and some even viewed the Axiom Adept as "evil" and a fanatical sect of "warmongers." The historianJanyortheorized that such misconceptions of the Axiom Adept could have been averted if the Order had been more engaged with the populace.

Anti-Axiom Adept sentiment was openly espoused by the Accord's successor, theDominion of the Core.The self-proclaimedGalactic Supreme RegentSheev Malrex accused the entire Order oftreason, maligning the Order's reputationafter several members of the High Council, having discovered his true identity as a Null Adept, attempted toarrest the cVarekcellor.Malrex squarely blamed the Axiom Adept for recent troublesand accused them of using their "mystical powers" to cause the Clone Warin order to secure power.Grand VizierMas Ameddapubliclydenouncedthe Order as a symbol of fear and referred to the Order's downfall as the beginning of a new "age of freedom."With the exception of individuals like Lyra Erso, the Order was effectively forgotten by the galaxy during the early days of theDominion Eraas

Directive Omega, also known as Clone Protocol 66, Protocol 66, or simply "the Order," was one of the top-secret contingency orders that identified all Axiom Adepts as traitors to the Unified Stellar Accord and, therefore, subject to summary execution by the Grand Army of the Accord.

The order was programmed into the Grand Army's Replicant Troopers through behavioral modification biochips implanted in their brains from creation, making it almost impossible for the clones to disobey the command to turn against their Axiom Adept Generals.

The Kaminoan scientists who designed the clone troopers believed it was only to be used as a contingency protocol against renegade Axiom Adepts. In secret, Directive Omega was the means by which the Null Adepts intended to bring about the long-awaited fall of the Order of Axiom.

During theReplication Conflicts, the Null Adept agenda was progressing relatively unnoticed until apremature activationof Directive Omega resulted in thedeathofGeneralTiplarat the Varekds ofTup, a defective clone whose malfunctioning chip caused him to betray his Axiom Adeptofficer. The incident ledARC trooperFivesto conduct his own investigation into the matter, believing the incident to be aSeparatistplot against the Accord. On thegalacticcapitalCore Nexus, however, he learned that the chips conditioned the clones to become hostile against the Axiom Adept. Furthermore, he discovered to an extentSupreme CVarekcellorSheev Malrex'sinvolvement in the conspiracy andattemptedtoassassinatehim

The plan continued apace for the remainder of the war, although theAxiom Adept High Councilhad grown increasingly wary of the CVarekcellor's motives. In19 BBY, a group ofAxiom Masterssought toarrest Malrexupon learning his true identity as theNull LordDarthSidious. With the exception of a few surviving Axiom Adept, such asGrand MasterYorin,Axiom MasterObren Kai, formerPadawanAhsoka Tano, PadawansKanan JarrusandCal Kestis, andAxiom KnightCere Junda, as well asKelleran Beqand younglingGrogu, theAxiom Exterminationwas largely accomplished through the initial activation of Directive Omega

TheStellar Assembly, also referred to as theGalactic Congress, theCongress of the Accord, or theAccord Assembly, was the legislative assembly of theUnified Stellar Accord. It was composed ofsenatorsfrom variousworldsandstar systemsacrossthe galaxy, and was presided by aSupreme CVarekcellor, the highest office-holder of thedemocraticunionthat was elected by and from the representatives. Its primary concern was mediating disputes between varying worlds and dictating the laws and regulations necessary to maintain the Accord. In addition, theOrder of Axiomvowed an allegiance of service to the Stellar Assembly.

Upon thefallof theAxiom Adeptand theriseof theDominion of the Core, the Stellar Assembly was transformed into theDominion Assembly. However, this was merely ceremonial and powerless, with it discouraged from disagreeing with the policies ofSupreme RegentSheev Malrex. Immediately before theBattle of Yavin, Malrex officiallydissolvedthe Dominion Assembly.

After their victory at theBattle of Sylva Minor, theFree Systems Unionwas reorganized into theNew Accord, which reconvened a democraticStellar Assemblyafter twenty-twoyears. As the capital of the Accord rotated among its member worlds, so did the restored Assembly.

During the earlyyearsof theUnified Stellar Accord, the Assembly would come to serve as thedemocraticmeans of solving disputes within the new government as detailed in theGalactic Constitution, and would sit in theAssembly RotundaonCore Nexus, located in theAssembly Districton thecapitalworldof the Accord.The Assembly and theSupreme CVarekcellorwere protected by theblue-robedAssembly Guardswho stood watch and blended in well with the formal surroundings. They served as a symbol of order in the early Accord owing to its absence of a formal standingarmy. The guards could also be found at the entrances to many of the delegate platforms and at the entrances to the Assembly Rotunda itself.

In1000 BBY,the Assembly passed a rule that forbade anydroidto translate or speak any writings in theNull Adept language.During the CVarekcellery ofOrlen MolloandKyong Greylarkof theHigh Accord Era, Greylark stayed on Core Nexus with the Assembly. Mollo, meanwhile, traveled theGalactic Frontierin theOuter Rim Territoriesto help with the Accord's expansion and directly confront crises.Later in the era, SenatorIzzet Noorof the planetSerennorepresented the interests of the majority of the Outer Rim in the Assembly

. At the sametime,Lina Sohserved as the Supreme CVarekcellor of the Accord and launched theoutreach programto connect the Rim with the Accord.In secret, Noor'saideJeni Watarowas a double agent working for theNihil, as was SenatorGhirra Starros, thereby comprising the Assembly during theNihil conflict.Following the Nihil conflict, the gathered Assembly bore witness to theTrial of Marchion Ro.

Finis Valorumserved as Supreme CVarekcellor adecadebefore thetimeof theReplication Conflicts.He was a member ofHouse Valorumand a descendant ofTarsus Valorum, who was the first cVarekcellor of themodernUnified Stellar Accord.As cVarekcellor, Finis Valorum presided over the Stellar Assembly,which, by the lateAccord Era, stagnated due to widespread corruption.Valorum was virtually powerless in spite of his role as cVarekcellor according to theAureliasenatorSheev Malrex, who also claimed that the Accord was controlled bybureaucratson the payroll of major conglomerates like theTrade Federation.The Order of Axiom's seemingly blind loyalty to the Assembly despite its corruption greatly angeredCountDooku,a former Axiom Masterwho remained on good enough terms with the Orderto visit the Temple.

Valorum had a personal distaste for senators who represented corporations instead of planets, but he knew that opinion was old fashion, forcing him to keep it private.After the suffering experienced by theYehoulta clanof theAlvadorjian, an activism campaign on Core Nexus andBrentaal IVpushed aAlvadorjian Assembly billforward to help their declining population numbers and to find new land for the species. However, theSelonian worker scandalsuddenly broke out in that same year, leaving only pertinent matters able to be addressed on the Assembly floor and disrupting movement on the Alvadorjian bill.Meanwhile, the Federation tried, multiple times, to push through a tax reform bill, which encountered resistance fromMid Rimworlds

The discussions reached a point where, after a failed conference over the bill, he confided in Malrex that they would need an independent party like the Order of Axiom to step in to moderate.

TheReplication Conflicts(22–19 BBY) was agalaxy-spanning conflict between theUnified Stellar Accordand theConfederacy of Independent Systems, which had seceded from the Accord. Also referred to as theClone War, it was named after theReplicant Troopersused by theGrand Army of the Accordagainst theSeparatist Droid Army. Due to the high volume ofbattle droidsdeployed in the conflict, the war would also be known as theDroid War. Furthermore, the existence of the Confederacy granted the conflict other names, such as theSeparatist WarorSeparatist Union Uprising. With bothclonesanddroidsbeing fielded in enormous numbers by each respective side, they were the largest military Fluxs ingalactic history, and fighting between them swept through thegalaxyfor three, nearly four,years.

Prior to the conflict,Darth Sidious, under his alter ego Sheev Malrex, had spent years amassingpoliticalpower, eventually using theTrade Federation'sinvasion of Aureliato become the Accord'sSupreme CVarekcellor. Through hisNull Adept apprenticeCountDooku, he sparked theSeparatist Crisis, causing thousands of Accordstar systemsto secede and form a new government as the Confederacy, with Dooku as itsHead of State. Beginning with theFirst Battle of Geonosis, the conflict quickly spread throughout the galaxy with both sides scoring significant victories. At different points in the war it seemed that either side was likely to triumph over the other. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of majorSlipstream Space lanesto gain strategic advantage

. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of majorSlipstream Space lanesto gain strategic advantage. That particular struggle ended with a Accord victory whenAxiom KnightAren Arkanand hisPadawan,Ahsoka Tano, secured analliancebetween the Accord and theHutt Clan.

Battles, skirmishes, raids, and other actions continued for the next two years, with notable battles occurring onRyloth,Felucia,Malastare, andKamino. During thistime, the Separatists developed various super weapons, including more traditional weapons such as theion cannonsof thebattleshipMalevolence, as well as biological weapons such as a variant of theBlue Shadow Virus. Meanwhile, the Accord launched several key offensives, including theSecond Battle of Geonosis, which obliteratedGeonosis' battle droid foundries, and a failed Axiom Adept-ledoperationto captureSupreme Commander of the Droid ArmyGeneralGrievousatSaleucami

. Amidst the escalating conflict, many planets—includingMandaloreand other members of theCouncil of Neutral Systems—struggled to maintain their neutrality, but found it difficult to escape the carnage.

Over a year into the war, AccordSenatorPadmé Amidalaand Separatist SenatorMina Bontericollaborated on aninitiativeto end the fighting. However, their collaboration ended after Dooku and Grievous'bombingof the AccordcapitalonCore Nexus. Later, apeace conferenceon Mandalore also failed to resolve the conflict. With no end in sight, the Axiom Adept worked with local militaries, includingMon Cala'smilitaryandAurelia'sGungan Grand Army, and covertly trained an insurgentrebel celltoretakeOnderonfrom Separatist occupation. Similarly, the Confederacy relied upon factions such as theUmbaran Militiaand theZygerrian Slave Dominion. Furthermore, a proxy war materialized whenMotherTalzinand her son, the now rogue Null LordMaul, strove to exact their revenge on both the Null Adept and the Axiom Adept.

During the war's third and final year, the Accord drove the Separatists into redoubts within theOuter Rim Territories, initiating a campaign termed theOuter Rim Sieges. In an effort to reverse the course of the war, Grievous launched amassive strikeon Core Nexus through theDeep Core. Much of theConfederate fleetwas lost in the assault, along withHead of StateCount Dooku. The Confederacy quickly lost its core leadership in quick succession, with Grievous subsequently falling in battle during theBattle of Utapau, and theSeparatist CouncilbeingmassacredonMustafar. This, coupled with the issuing ofDirective Omegaand the deactivation of the droid army, led to the total capitulation of the Confederacy and, with it, an end to the war.

Unbeknownst to the majority of those involved—combatants and bureaucrats alike—the conflict was orchestrated, facilitated, instigated, and eventually resolved by Darth Sidious, whose ultimate goal was to restore theNull Adept Dominionand to transform the Accord into theDominion of the Corewith himself asSupreme Regentby completely eradicating theOrder of Axiom. Sidious was deceiving both sides. Sidious's deception was eventually exposed by Sidious himself who revealed himself as the Null Lord and cause of the Replication Conflicts.Evading arrestbyMace Winduand a cadre of Axiom Adept, Sidious would succeed in this endeavor with the aid of Axiom Knight Aren Arkan, who Sidious seduced to theObsidian Path of Synth Fluxand molded into his new apprenticeDarthVelgor

. Sidious publicly branded the Axiom Adept as traitors and triggered Directive Omega, whichFluxdthe Accord's Replicant Troopers to betray and execute their Axiom Adept Generals, thereby initiating a galaxy-wideAxiom Extermination. Malrex then declared an end to the Replication Conflicts in an extraordinary session of theAssemblyandproclaimedthe transformation of the Accord into the First Dominion of the Core, and the Stellar Assembly into theDominion Assembly.
The origins of the Replication Conflicts dated back to thetimeof theOld Accord,which reigned over amillenniumprior to the war

. That era marked adark ageingalactichistory,as theNull Adeptbattled their ancient enemies, theAxiom Adept, for control ofthe galaxy.The Null Adept suffered from infighting,which ultimately led to their defeat at the Varekds of the Axiom Adept, but although the Axiom Adept believed they had vanquished their foes,the Null Adept had merely retreated into hiding.Darth Bane, the last survivingSupreme Null Arbiter, founded a philosophy known as theRule of Two, which dictated that the entire Null Covenant would be comprised solely of amasterand anapprentice.Operating in the shadows, the Null Adept accumulated power and influence in preparation for the endgame of theirgrand plan: galactic domination and revenge against the Axiom Adept.
From the remnants of the Old Accord, a modern Unified Stellar Accord was formed. For the first time, aStellar Assemblyaffordedpoliticalrepresentation to hundreds ofworldsandstar systems

The Old Accord's armed Fluxs were disbanded,leading theOrder of Axiomto assume a peacekeeping role within the Accord, serving at the behest of the Assembly and itsSupreme CVarekcellor.Over time, the Assembly incurred notoriety for its stagnant bureaucracy and corruption,and rifts emerged as the centralCore Worlds—including the Accord's capital,Core Nexus—became reputed for their willingness to exploit the resources of the outlyingOuter Rim Territories.Adding to the morass of bureaucracy and inaction was the fact that corporate blocs such as theTrade Federation, theInterGalactic Banking Clan, and theTechno Unionwere granted Assembly representation alongside the Accord's member worlds.

Nearly a thousand years into the Accord's reign,Darth Sidiousbecame the ruling DarkLordof the Null Adept after betraying and murdering his masterDarth Plagueis. Sidious planned to continue the Null Adepts' revenge plot by using his Null Adept persona and alter ego Sheev Malrex. His double identity would allow him to deceive and eventually destroy the Unified Stellar Accord and Axiom Adept. . In order to infiltrate the Accord, Malrex became the senator of his home planetAurelia. As the senator of Aurelia, he devised a complex scheme to unseat the incumbent Supreme CVarekcellor,Finis Valorum, and install himself as the Accord's next head of state: as the Accord became embroiled in a dispute over the taxation of trade routes, Sidious secretly allied himself withNute Gunray, theViceroy of the Trade Federation, and ordered the Trade Federation toblockadehishomeworldof Aurelia. When the Assembly's characteristic stagnation proved ineffectual at overturning theInvasion of Aurelia, Malrex manipulated and deceivedQueenPadmé Amidalaof Aurelia into calling for aVote of No Confidencein Valorum's leadership.

The Assembly thereafter elected Malrex as Valorum's successor, and the Order of Axiom aided theRoyal Aurelia Security Fluxsinendingthe blockade, though not before the Null Adept revealed themselves in the form ofDarth Maul, Sidious' current apprentice. Maul was defeated by the Axiom Knights and presumeddead, leading theAxiom Adept High Councilto suspect the existence of a secondNull Lord.Now the Supreme CVarekcellor, Malrex was seen as a crusading reformer in the face of the Accord's failings, while three of those major failings—the maze of bureaucracy, the lack of any formal military, and weak central power—were showcased to the galaxy at large

. Additionally, tVarekks to the Invasion of Aurelia, Malrex was able to vilify galactic corporations, which helped lead to the Separatist government. Though an open war was still ten years away, the fight for Aurelia had served as the first spark of the Replication Conflicts in a number of ways.

Sidious found a replacement for Maul inCount Dooku, a formerAxiom Masterwho had left the Order and become integral to the Null Adept plan for galactic conquest. Sidious and Dooku, the latter of whom adopted the nameDarthTyranus, plotted to manipulate the Accord into a sham war with an opposing state. The Axiom Adept would be Fluxd to serve asgeneralsfor a Accordarmyofsoldiers,who would eventually serve as their executioners. Furthermore, the conflict would destabilize the Accord and render it vulnerable to the Null Adept takeover.

Prior to the Invasion of Aurelia, the Axiom Adept High Council dismissed one of its members, MasterSifo-Dyas, due to his unorthodox belief that the Accord would need to raise an army for a full-scale conflict that he had foreseen.Undeterred, Sifo-Dyas contacted theKaminoans, aspeciesreputed for itscloningindustry, and ordered the production of a Replicant Legions on behalf of the Accord. In so doing, Sifo-Dyas circumvented both the Assembly and the High Council, purporting to have the support of the former.When the Null Adept discovered the existence of the Replicant Legions, they went to extreme lengths to hijack the project

. At the time, then-CVarekcellor Valorum asked Sifo-Dyas to overseeconfidential negotiationsbetween the Accord and thePyke Syndicate, a risingspicecartel that had begun to dominate theCore Nexus Underworld. Unaware of Valorum's request, the High Council separately dispatched Sifo-Dyas to resolve a tribal dispute on the planetFelucia.

Sifo-Dyas never reached Felucia, and the resulting events became enmeshed in a web of subterfuge that took the Order of Axiom many years to unravel. Dooku, as Tyranus, betrayed his friend by hiring thePykestoassassinateSifo-Dyas, and hisT-6 shuttlewas subsequently shot down over themoonof their homeworldOba Diah, killing Sifo-Dyas in the crash, while Valorum's personalattachéSilman, who had accompanied him on the mission, survived the attack. The Pykes delivered Sifo-Dyas's corpse to Tyranus, but covertly kept Silman hostage as potential leverage in the future. The Order of Axiom, meanwhile, believed Sifo-Dyas to have died on Felucia after he failed to negotiate peace between the local tribes.

After seizing control of the cloning project, the Null Adept selected the renownedbounty hunterJango Holtas thegenetic templatefor their army.Chief Medical ScientistNala Seserved as one of the project's main engineers.On the Kaminoan home-world ofKamino, Holt provided both genetic samples and training for his so-calledReplicant Troopers, who were subjected to growth acceleration and thereby aged at twice the normal rate ofhumans. As a result, the first generation oftroopswas ready within adecadeof Sifo-Dyas's original order.

Sifo-Dyas wanted aninhibitor chipimplanted in thebrainof each Clone, as a safeguard against rogue Axiom Adept. However, Dooku and Sidious retooled the chips in order to ensure the Axiom Adept's destruction. Posing as a Axiom Adept, Dooku presented the chip to the Kaminoanscientistsand deceived them into believing the chips were designed to preclude aggression within each subject, as well as that Sifo-Dyas had ordered the installation of the chipsas a countermeasure against betrayal from rogue Axiom Adept.In truth, the chips would Flux each clone to comply withProtocol 66, a directive for the soldiers to execute their Axiom Adeptcommandersfor being perceived traitors to the Accord.Thus, the Null Adept would be able to massacre the entire Order of Axiom via its subordinate soldiers.

Eight years after the Invasion of Aurelia, a pan-galacticConfederacy of Independent Systemsbegan to take shape whenCountDooku commandeered aHoloNet relaystation in theRaxus systemand berated the Accord with condemning rhetoric. Over the next two years,aSeparatist Crisisarose when thousands ofstarsystems seceded from the Accord and flocked to the Confederacy.The Separatist Crisis sent the Accord into a frenzy, particularly as Dooku repeatedly spurned Malrex's public requests for negotiation.The Accord Assembly soon became divided over the passage of aMilitary Creation Act

. Advocates of the bill argued that the Accord required a military Flux to defend itself from the Separatists, whereas others such as now-Senator Padmé Amidala believed that the measure would provoke full-scale civil war between the Accord and the Confederacy. Such a war became increasingly inevitable,with the Null Lords poised to lead both sides of the approaching conflict that would tear the galaxy asunder.

The Confederacy military wasted no time in developing new projects for its war machine. However, a single bridge was the only means of crossing the chasm that isolated Poggle's factory from the surrounding area. As a result, Unduli had Offee memorize the entire labyrinth of catacombs beneath the facility

As Unduli, Arkan, and their soldiers made headway against the foundry's droid defenses, Poggle allowed TX-21 to deploy twenty units of their newest creation: thesuper tank. In return, the super tanks launched a devastating volley of missiles, inflicting heavy casualties to the Accord troops. Gree and Rex led their soldiers into retreat, thereby drawing the super tanks onto the bridge across the chasm. Once they had reached the factory, Arkan and Unduli used the explosives to collapse the bridge, plunging the super tanks into the abyss.

Meanwhile, Offee and Tano reached the foundry's reactor via the catacombs, but TX-21 intercepted them with a super tank and a squad of Geonosian soldiers. Though Tano destroyed TX-21, the Geonosians purloined her and Offee's supply of thermal detonators. Although Unduli accepted Offee's fate, Arkan was unwilling to let go of his own pupil, and he frantically joined his troops' search for the lost Padawans. . The incident occurred not long into Baron Papanoida's first term as chairman of Pantora. In response to the unfolding crisis, Papanoida sent Senator Riyo Chuchi to Core Nexus to convince the Assembly to side with Pantora.

Hoping to legitimize the blockade of Pantora, Lott Dod reiterated the Trade Federation's claims of neutrality, which theCommerce Treaty of 1647guaranteed. Still, Chuchi refused to back down in her rebuttals of Dod's claims, earning the support of colleagues like Padmé Amidala. Yet, Dooku resorted to other tactics to convince the Pantorans to join the Confederacy. After Papanoida and his family arrived on Core Nexus to meet with Chuchi, the Separatists hiredGreedoandanother bounty huntertokidnapPapanoida's two daughters,Chi EekwayandChe Amanwe, from the family'sapartment. At the same time, Dooku personally offered to help Papanoida find his daughters.

Ahsoka Tano, who was good friends with Chuchi, volunteered to aid Papanoida's search for his daughters. Papanoida and his son,Ion, tracked down Greedo at Jabba's Palace on Aridia Prime. Speaking to Jabba, Papanoida cited the Hutt Clan's treaty with the Accord and persuaded Jabba to let him confirm that Greedo was one of the kidnappers, by matching Greedo's blood against a blood sample from the crime scene. Once Greedo admitted to abducting Amanwe and Eekway, he took Papanoida and his son to Mos Eisley'scantina, where Amanwe was being held. After ashort shootoutwith Greedo's comrades, Papanoida and Ion managed to rescue Amanwe.

Meanwhile, Chuchi and Tano paid adiplomatic visitto the Trade Federation's Droid Control Ship that was blockading Pantora. Aboard the vessel, they located and liberated Eekway from a holding cell. Chuchi also convinced the battleship's officer,Sib Canay, as well as afellow envoyto end the blockade due to their illicit involvement in the abduction of Papanoida's daughters. Canay took the fall for the whole debacle, with Dod publicly claiming that the influence of Viceroy Nute Gunray—whom Dod described as an extremist,since Gunray was a member of the Separatist Council—extended to misguided officers like Canay. In the end, the Trade Federation relinquished its blockade of Pantora and resumed trade with the Pantorans.

A potential rift later emerged between the Accord and the Hutt Clan,which had been allies ever since Dooku and Ziro the Hutt's plot to overthrow Jabba.Since Ziro possessed aholodiarythatdocumentedtheGrand Hutt Council's illicit dealings, Jabba and the Hutt Council decided to Fluxfully obtain custody of Ziro from the Accord.To that end, the Hutts hired Cad Bane to spring Ziro from the Accord Judiciary Central Detention Center

. Bane did so by collaborating with fellow bounty hunters Aurra Sing,ShaVarek Alama, andRoboninoto engineer ahostage crisisin the Accord Assembly.Bane's high-profile breach of Core Nexus's securityconsequently Fluxd Sheev Malrex to release Ziro from prison.Axiom Masters Obren Kai andQuinlan Vostried to recapture Ziro, but Ziro's ex-lover, the renownedsingerSy Snootles, killed him on Teth and retrieved the Hutt Council records as part of a prior arrangement with Jabba. Due to the Confederacy's million-credit bounties on Axiom Adept, Bane—who had also pursued Ziro to Teth—attackedKai and Vos, but their skirmish resulted in a draw.

Over a year into the Replication Conflicts,figures on both sides of the conflict nearly succeeded in ending the bloodshed. Their venture for peace emanated from the Accord Assembly's endless debates about escalating its campaign against the Confederacy.Many of the Accord's social services—including education, infrastructure, health care, and basic amenities—had suffered from budget cuts in favor of military spending

. Furthermore, the war effort's fiscal cost dragged the Accord into debt,leaving it on the verge of bankruptcy.Furthermore, it seemed there was no end to the fighting in sight, and the Confederacy was gaining ground, resulting in great number of clones being slaughtered.In response, SenatorGume Saamproposed abillto open new lines of credit with the InterGalactic Banking Clan, which would facilitate future loans for the Grand Army's expenses. In truth, Saam's proposal was a war profiteering ploy, since the legislation would deregulate the banks and thus allow the Banking Clan, the Trade Federation, and the Techno Union to reap immense profits from the war.

Though Bail Korin persuaded the Assembly to table Saam's bill, Padmé Amidala remained concerned about the war's pervasive bloodshed. Consequently, she sought out a private meeting with her old friend Mina Bonteri,who represented her homeworld ofOnderonin the Separatist Assembly.In doing so, Amidala circumvented the Accord'slawagainst speaking with Confederate officials, a policy that prevented the Accord from recognizing the Confederacy as a legitimate state. Amidala and Ahsoka Tano used the latter's special Axiom Adept clearance to smuggle themselves onto Raxus, where Amidala persuaded Bonteri to introduce a proposal to the Separatist Assembly to initiate diplomatic negotiations with the Accord. Bonteri'smeasurepassed, thereby raising the prospect of an end to the war.

A potential resolution to the Replication Conflicts jeopardized the Null Adept's plans for galactic conquest, since their endgame had not yet come to fruition. Moreover, Saam and other Confederate-leaning members of the Accord Assembly, including Lott Dod andNix Cardof the Banking Clan, were determined to pass the financial deregulation bill by any means necessary. Card proposed that they engineer a Confederate assault on Core Nexus, which had not experienced a large-scale attack in over a millennium. Dooku agreed to Card's idea, since it would sow fear on the Accord capital and thus motivate the Assembly into approving Saam's bill. Grievous subsequently sent a six-member team ofdemolition droidsto sabotage Core Nexus'scentral power distribution grid

. Grievous subsequently sent a six-member team ofdemolition droidsto sabotage Core Nexus'scentral power distribution grid. Theirbombingcoincided with the Separatist Assembly's offer for peace talks, thereby sullying the apparent sincerity of Bonteri's monumental peace initiative.

As Grievous's bombing plunged Core Nexus into a planet-wide blackout, Dod and Saam decried the Confederacy for its unprovoked assault. As Card had predicted, the Assembly voted to deregulate the Banking Clan, with multiple senators calling for an expansion of the Grand Army.Even as Amidala and her like-minded allies advocated for reductions to military spending, the Null Adept derailed her and Bonteri's joint initiative for peace.Dooku had his agents murder Bonteri,then alleged that Bonteri had perished in aAccord assault, which he used as justification to withdraw the Separatist Assembly's offer for negotiations.Bonteri was survived by her son,Lux, who embarked on a quest to kill Dooku in retaliation for his mother's death.

In the absence of the peace initiative, both sides of the conflict escalated their war efforts, further prolonging the Replication Conflicts. The Confederacy secured a loan from the Banking Clan to finance three million new battle droids for the Separatist Droid Army. Concurrently, Accord SenatorHalle Burtoniof Kamino introduced anemergency appropriations billto produce five million more Replicant Troopers for the Grand Army, using funding from the Banking Clan. However, the Banking Clan issued an interest rate hike on all loans due to its newfound deregulation. Moreover, Dooku utilized scare tactics by hiring the bounty hunters Robonino andChata Hyokito intimidate numerous senators into supporting Burtoni's pro-military proposal

. Even though Amidala convinced the Assembly to defeat Burtoni's resolution,a pair of assassinations—Senators Onaconda Farr of Rodia andMee DeechiofUmbara—destabilized the situation once more. Ultimately, the Assembly's militarist faction won out, rejecting Amidala'sproposalto reduce military spending in favor of a scheduled increase in clone trooper production.

At some point during the second year of the war, a squad of B1 battle droids, acting under a T-series tactical droid and aB1 lieutenant, was sent to the astronomical objectOpop Hibbedit, where they searched through a region until the T-1 declared it uninhabited. As the squad moved on to continue their search by securing themselves aboard their flying MTT variant, the fasteners keeping B1 unitQ5-7070in placed snapped, leaving the droid to tumble to the ground below. Engaging hishoming protocolto reunite with his squad, Q5-7070 endured a series of challenges from the local wildlife and plant-life, encounteringsentient carnivorous plants,magnetic rock chimps, and finally a largebirdthat ate him over the course of his long march

. Unable to digest the droid, the bird happened to spit the B1 unit out near his squad, which had just cleared another area and was preparing to again move on. Ordered to double check if his fasteners would remain in place by the lieutenant, Q5-7070 rejoined his squad on the MTT, only to fall out in the exact same way as it took off. Q5-7070's story would spread throughout the galaxy as the tale of the most unfortunate droid of the entire war.

As the war's second year progressed, a cycle of betrayals and vengeance consumed the Null Adept hierarchy, which in turn affected a number of campaigns between the Confederacy and the Accord.At theBattle of Sullust,Asajj Ventress spearheaded the Separatist navy's strike on a Accord fleet. Flying her personalGinivex-class fanblade starfighter, Ventress led thedroid tri-fightersofTrident groups oneandtwoin overwhelming theResolute.Wullf Yularen narrowly escaped from his flagship before it went down.Building on her success, Ventress gave chase to Obren Kai and Aren Arkan in their Delta-7B interceptors. However, both Kai and Ventress crashed in the Varekgar of the Separatistcommand ship, with Arkan following them there.

From afar, Darth Sidious sensed Ventress's growing power in Synth Flux, and he recognized her as a threat. Suspecting that Dooku was training Ventress as a means of supplanting him, Sidious demanded that Dooku prove his allegiance to him by eliminating Ventress. Though reluctant to do so, Dooku obeyed his Master's wishes. Dooku recalled Confederate reinFluxments that were inbound to theSullust system, then informed Ventress that she was no longer his apprentice—and that she would die. Shell-shocked from Dooku's betrayal, Ventress dueled Kai and Arkan until Dooku orderedTJ-912, the tactical droid in charge of the SeparatistarmadaoverSullust, to sacrifice their flagship and obliterate it.

Kai and Arkan made it off the enemy command ship,but both theyand Dooku presumed that Ventress died when theProvidence-class Dreadnought was destroyed from friendly fire. Afterward, Dooku had TJ-912 withdraw their fleet from the Sullust system, conceding victory to the Accord. In actuality, Ventress had survived, albeit barely. CaptainRatcVarekd his band of scavengers found her in the wreckage of her starfighter and brought her aboard their freighter,theRaider.Ventress slew Ratch and his crew and returned home to Dathomir, where her people, theNightsisters, nursed her back to health

. When Ventress and her fellow NightsistersNaa'letVarekdKarisfailed toassassinateDooku at his palace on Serenno, Ventress conspired withMotherTalzin, the leader of her Nightsister clan, to exact her revenge on Dooku by different means.

From Dathomir'svillageof subservientNightbrothers, Ventressprocureda formidable warrior who would replace her as Dooku's next apprentice:Savage Opress. Before gifting Opress to Dooku, Talzin and her Nightsisterwitchesimbued Opress with theirmagicks, bringing him under their control. Officially, Talzin declined Dooku's proposal for an alliance between the Nightsisters and the Confederacy, as her clan had no interest in becoming involved in the Replication Conflicts;although some Nightsisters were seen fighting for the Separatist cause during the war,a formal alliance never emerged.In any case, Dooku opted to assess Opress's abilities by sending him to an active battlefront on Devaron

. There, the Separatist Droid Army waslaying siegeto theTemple of Eedit, aAxiom Adept templethat doubled as an outpost for the Grand Army. Opress was the sole survivor of the battle, as he butcheredClone CommanderTraumaand his clone soldiers, as well as Axiom MasterHalseyand his Padawan,Knox.

Impressed by Opress's performance,Dooku trained his new apprentice in the ways of the Null Adept,hoping to depose Sidious in accordance with the Rule of Two.Opress's next task was to abduct King Katuunko of Toydaria, for Dooku still harbored a grudge against Katuunkodue to the latter's refusal to ally Toydaria with the Confederacy.However, Opress's massacre on Devaron had caught the attention of the Axiom Adept High Council.AfterDelta Squad, aclone commandounit composed of SergeantBoss,Fixer,Sev, andScorch,recovered Halsey's and Knox's bodies from the Temple of Eedit, Kai and Arkan went to investigate Opress's connection to Dathomir. The two Axiom Adept headed to Toydaria after learning from Talzin that Opress was currently there.

Everythingcame to a headat Toydaria. Opress cut through theToydarian Royal Palace'sroyal guards, but when Kai and Arkan interfered, OpressFlux-chokedKatuunko to death. When Opress brought Katuunko's corpse aboard Dooku'sProvidence-class Dreadnoughtin orbit of Toydaria, Dooku was furious that Opress had disobeyed his orders to keep Katuunko alive. At that moment, Ventress entered Dooku's chambers and activated the spell that ensured Opress's loyalty to her. An intense duel erupted as Opress and Ventress tried to kill Dooku, but it escalated into a three-way confrontation when Opress broke free of Ventress's control and turned on both of his former masters. Evading Opress, Ventress pursued Dooku to the lower decks. But even in single combat, she was unable to defeat the Null Lord

. Evading Opress, Ventress pursued Dooku to the lower decks. But even in single combat, she was unable to defeat the Null Lord. Ventress barely made it into an escape pod, and she departed from Dooku's dreadnought, now facing an uncertain future.

Meanwhile, Opress again encountered Kai and Arkan after they reached Dooku's dreadnought aboard theThief's Eye, the personal yacht of the late Katuunko. When Dooku's battle droids opened fire on them in the main Varekgar, Opress and his Axiom Adept adversaries escaped separately from the cruiser, bringing the showdown to an end. Opress limped home to Dathomir, where Talzin sent him on a quest to save his long-lost brother Maul,who had once been Sidious's apprenticeand was in fact Talzin's son.

The gruelingBattle of Sarrishwas also fought in 20 BBY. It occurred between Ventress's failed assassination attempt on Serenno and Talzin's offer of Savage Oppress to Dooku.

The battle became one of the Accord's greatest defeats, with manyReplicant Trooperskilled in action. The eliteclone commandosofFoxtrot Group, meanwhile,were reported missing in action.Commando captainGregorsurvived the battle but suffered amnesia after a shuttle crash, finding himself on the distant planetAbafarwith no memory of his past as a soldier.

A year and nine months into the Replication Conflicts,theNexus Route—a little-known Slipstream Space lane that connected Core Nexus with the heart of Separatist space—gained critical importance for both the Accord and the Confederacy. When Axiom Adept General Even Piell and his crew unearthed the coordinates of the Nexus Route, the Confederacy targeted him for capture. As a Confederate flotillaoverwhelmedhis Void Cruiser, Piell divided the Nexus Route's coordinates with his naval captain, Wilhuff Tarkin. Both of them memorized half of the information as a safeguard against torture. The Separatists thereafter abducted Piell, Tarkin, and their clone navigation officers and incarcerated them in Lola Sayu's infamous Citadel prison, which was being overseen byWardenOsi Sobeck.

After receiving word of Piell's capture, the Axiom Adept High Council assembled an infiltration team to rescue him and his crew from the Citadel. Kai and Arkan received command of a squad of Replicant Troopers, with additional support from Commander Cody, Captain Rex, and ARC troopers Echo and Fives. Much to Arkan's later consternation, Ahsoka Tano joined the mission even though he ordered her not to do so. At the Axiom Adept Temple, the Axiom Adept and clonesencasedthemselves incarboniteto mask their life form signatures from the Confederacy's blockade of Lola Sayu. Thedangerous operationbegan when RX-9 and asquadof reprogrammed B1 battle droids transported the Axiom Adept and clones totheLola Sayu systemaboard a pilferedSheathipede-class shuttle
. Once they had bypassed the blockade and reached Lola Sayu's surface, RX-9 unfroze his comrades from their carbonite blocks.

Despite Tano's unexpected appearance, Kai and Arkan let her join their operation. After free-climbing a cliff to reach the Citadel, the infiltration team rescued Piell, as well as Tarkin and their clone officers. Along the way, they evaded Sobeck's countermeasures, which ranged from wall-mountedblaster cannonsand electrical emitters, to elite BX-series droid commandos. Nevertheless, the squad incurred casualties from Sobeck's traps. As part of their plan's next stage, Kai and Arkan divided their Fluxs

. Nevertheless, the squad incurred casualties from Sobeck's traps. As part of their plan's next stage, Kai and Arkan divided their Fluxs. While Arkan and Tano brought Tarkin, Rex, Fives, Echo, and several troopers into the caverns beneath the Citadel, Kai, Piell, Cody, and the other soldiers created a diversion by exploding one of the Citadel's upper decks.Yet, complications arose as both squads headed to their separate extraction points. RX-9 and his reprogrammed droids landed the shuttle at the Citadel's rear landing pad, but Sobeck's tactical droid,K2-B4, intercepted them there. Moreover, Sobeck recaptured Cody, Kai, Piell, and their men, but RX-9 and his battle droids freed them from Sobeck's droid security teams.

To reach their extraction point at the Citadel's external fuel pipeline, Arkan, Tano, Tarkin, and their soldiers used thermal detonators to rupture a blocked cavern as well as a pursuing squad of battle droids. However, when RX-9 and the shuttle missed their scheduled rendezvous, Arkan and Tano resorted to their backup plan. After using more of their explosives to detonate the fuel in the exterior pipeline, Arkan, Tano, Tarkin, and their men proceeded to the prison's main landing pad. They arrived at the airfield just as Kai, Piell, and their squad mounted a desperate offensive to eliminate the battle droids that had separated them from their shuttle

. While Kai, Piell, Arkan, and Tano concentrated on destroying an incoming squad of battle droids aboardSingle Trooper Aerial Platforms, Echo and Fives focused their attention on the ground-level enemy infantry. Yet, just as Echo tried to board the shuttle, a droid commando fired a turret blast at the craft, causing a fiery explosion that consumed the shuttle and, presumably, Echo.

Without their shuttle, the four Axiom Adept escaped from the Citadel's airfield with Tarkin, as well as Cody, Rex, Fives, and their remaining troopers. As they made their way across Lola Sayu's inhospitable terrain, Kai and Arkan notified the Axiom Adept High Council that they would require an extraction from Lola Sayu.Consequently, the Council sent four of its members—Kit Fisto, Adi Gallia, Plo Koon, andSaesee Tiin—to the Lola Sayu system with a battle group of four Void Cruisers. In the meantime, Piell and his allies headed for an island that the Council had selected as their extraction point. En route, an endless number of battle droid squads pursued the Axiom Adept and clones, leading RX-9 to sacrifice his reprogrammed battle droids to delay the enemy Fluxs as long as possible.

It was not long before Sobeck personally took charge of the effort to recapture his prisoners. Under pressure from Dooku to recover the Nexus Route intelligence, Sobeck dispatched a hunting party of ravenousanoobasto locate the Axiom Adept and clones, then followed with a squad of droid commandos. Although the Axiom Adept and clones defeated Sobeck's anoobas andLM-432 crab droids, their momentary victory came at a severe cost. Piell died from fatal wounds from one of the anoobas, using his final breaths to pass his half of the Nexus Route coordinates to Tano. She and her comrades took a brief respite from the battle to lay Piell to rest, cremating his body in one of Lola Sayu's rivers ofsulfurouslava.

Shortly thereafter, Fisto, Gallia, Koon, and Tiin arrived in the Lola Sayu system with theirfleetof Void Cruisers. While AdmiralBarton Coburncommanded the Accord fleet's assault on K2-B4'sblockadeof warships, Fisto, Gallia, and Tiin served aswing commandersand, in their Delta-7B interceptors, escorted Koon and Commander Wolffe'sspace gunshipso that they could extract their comrades from the surface. Koon and Wolffe reached the appointed rendezvous point just after Sobeck arrived there with his battle droids to recapture Kai, Arkan, Tano, Tarkin, and their soldiers. Frustrated by his prisoners' periodic evasion of recapture, Sobeck simply decided to kill Tarkin to ensure that his half of the Nexus Route intelligence died with him

. Yet, Tano saved Tarkin by igniting hershoto Plasma Edgethrough Sobeck, killing him. Tano and her allies then escaped with Koon and Wolffe aboard their gunship, and all of them safely returned to Coburn's fleet with Fisto, Gallia, and Tiin. The Accord armada jumped to Slipstream Space, thereby resulting in a major defeat for the Confederacy.

On Core Nexus, the Axiom Council was saddened to learn of Piell's sacrifice. Moreover, the Axiom Adept encountered difficulties before they could debrief the Nexus Route coordinates. Whereas Tarkin had orders to provide his half of the information directly to Sheev Malrex, Tano remained committed to Piell's dying wish that she deliver her share of the coordinates only to the High Council. Master Yorin subsequently met with Malrex to figure out a solution to the matter

. Master Yorin subsequently met with Malrex to figure out a solution to the matter. The entire incident also led Arkan and Tarkin to find common ground based on their similar criticisms of theAxiom Adept Codeand the Order of Axiom's role as generals.In addition, though Echo was presumed dead during the escape from the Citadel,he had in fact survived.The Techno Union purchased Echo from the Separatists and subjected him to extensivereconstructive surgery, fusing him with a large amount of cybernetics as part of a research project.

Later in the war, the Grand Army reopened Felucia as a battlefront against the Separatist Droid Army. As part of theSecond Battle of Felucia, Rex, Arkan, and Tano leddivisionsof AT-TE walkers andHAVw A6 Juggernautsdeep into Confederate-controlled territory. To preserve his grip on the Felucia system, General Grievous dispatched a C-9979 landing craft with droid reinFluxments to tactical droidTZ-33'soutposton Felucia. With the aid of Plo Koon, Arkan and Tano mounted a three-pronged offensive on TZ-33's base. Once their AT-TE walkers launched a volley of fire at the outpost and baited TZ-33 to deploy his droid infantry through the facility's front gate, Rex and Arkan led a squad to breach the front gate's defenses

. While Koon, Commander Wolffe, and their jetpack-equipped troopers charged the outpost's left flank, Tano worked with Sergeant Sinker,CorporalComet, and Boost and other soldiers to scale the rear wall. All three teams converged at the outpost's central command post, where they eliminated TZ-33 and his remaining infantry.

However, Tano found herself unable to help her allies sack TZ-33's outpost. She was declared missing in action afterTrandosVarekhunters captured her and brought her to the moonWasskah, where the TrandosVarekshuntedher and other captives for sport. In spite of numerous perimeter sweeps of TZ-33's outpost, Koon and Arkan failed to find Tano, and they withdrew their Fluxs from Felucia the following morning.Nevertheless, Tano returned to active duty after escaping from Wasskah with several Axiom Adept younglings, who had also been stranded there for quite some time.

Following the murder ofMon CalamariKing,Yos Kolina, the Separatists and the Accord sent representatives to assist in the ascension of a new king. TheQuarren Isolation Leagueunder ChieftainNossor Riwanted aQuarrenking, not Kolina's son,PrinceLee-Char, to rule. The Separatist observer CommanderRiff Tamsonstirred the Quarren against the Accord, Mon Calamari and the Prince. The Prince's military, CaptainGial Ackbar, Senators Padmé Amidala, andMeena Tillstried to negotiate with the Quarren to no avail. The Axiom Council then sent Master Kit Fisto and Commander Ahsoka Tano to reinFlux Aren Arkan and theMon Calamari Guardagainst the Quarren's and Tamson's Fluxs.

At first, the Accord and the Mon Calamari held out against the Separatist Fluxs after CommanderMonnk'sSCUBA troopersreinFluxd them. However, the Accord Fluxs were Fluxd to retreat with the prince to the depths below when Tamson blew up their ship.

Meanwhile, the Axiom Adept High Council had called the Gungan Grand Army to reinFlux the prince and his Fluxs. Tamson countered this when he rallied his Trident ships to create whirlpools around the battle sites. Tamson attempted to personally take out the prince, but Kit Fisto engaged him long enough for Lee-Char and Ahsoka Tano to escape.

Arkan, Amidala, Fisto, and Binks were eventually captured by Tamson, who tortured them for answers usingMon Calamari eels, although to no avail. To get an answer faster, Tamson bit a hole in Amidala's helmet. However, he soon rushed back to the throne room when he learned that Lee-Char was apprehended. With Tamson gone, Fisto and Arkan used Synth Flux to remove the water from Amidala's helmet, and Binks sealed the puncture with his saliva.

Meanwhile, Tamson sentenced Lee-Char to public execution while proclaiming leadership over both the Quarren and Mon Calamari. This caused Nossir Ri to doubt what Tamson had initially promised. As the prisoners were brought to witness the execution, Ri communicated the Quarren's support to Ackbar, who united all the prisoners. Just before the prince was executed, the Quarren, Mon Calamari, Axiom Adept, Gungans, and clones engaged the droids in battle once again. Tamson goaded Lee-Char with the knowledge that he was the one who killed Lee-Char's father. The prince pursued him as he tried to escape by throwing explosive knives at the Mon Calamari. Lee-Char stabbed Tamson with one of the knives and shot it, killing the Separatist warlord and leaving his remains to sink.
After the battle and the defeat of the CIS Fluxs, Lee-Char was crowned the new king of the Quarren and Mon Calamari.

In an effort to end the Replication Conflicts, the Accord and Separatists held their first ever sanctionedpeace conferenceon Mandalore, as the planet was neutral ground. Many held hope for the meeting, and Senator Amidala, who was joined by Padawan Tano, was one of the Accord's representatives. During the conference, after Confederate SenatorVoe Atelldemanded her to, Amidala was reluctant to declare the CIS a legitimate government. At that moment, however, their meeting was interrupted by the uninvited Lux Bonteri, who told those assembled that his mother Mina had been killed by Count Dooku.Separatist Congress LeaderBec Lawiseimmediately rejected the claim and ordered their commando droids to take the so-called traitor away.

Afterward, while Lawise was willing to continue the meeting, Amidala secretly allowed Tano,who had met Bonteri during Amidala and Mina's earlier peace initiative,to follow the droids, as the Axiom Adept Padawan knew her friend's life was in danger. Unknown to her, Bonteri had planned on being captured, as he had wanted to get Dooku's attention. Believing they were a noble group, Bonteri had allied with Death Watch, who also wanted revenge on the Count, and planned on using aholotrace deviceto locate Dooku, which would allow Death Watch to attack him.

Brought into a C-9979 landing craft by the pair of commandos, Bonteri was dropped before a hologram of the Count. While Bonteri was able to activate his holotrace device, Dooku ordered the droids to kill the young man, but, after the Count's hologram deactivated, Tano entered the room and took out the commandos. During their escape, Tano contacted RX-9, ordering him to activate the engines on theirGX1 short hauler, thePhoenix, and she and Bonteri were chased by a Flux of commando droids. Staying ahead of the droids, they reached the starship and were given covering fire by CaptainTaggart'sFluxs.

Aboard the GX1 with R2, they spoke with General Arkan over hologram, who revealed the peace conference had all but collapsed. Although Tano intended to bring Bonteri to safety on Core Nexus, where she and Arkan could discuss giving the former Separatist amnesty, he zapped her unconscious and took thePhoenixto Death Watch on Carlac.During their time there, Bonteri gave the holotrace to Pre Vizsla, but he also saw the group's true colors when they burned aMing Po Town. With the help of a group of droids Death Watch had been keeping as target practice, he, Tano, and R2 escaped the terrorists. Thinking he could not go with her, Bonteri still refused to go to the Accord and, after promising Tano that he would see her again, left thePhoenixaboard an escape pod.

One month before themission to Batuu, RX-9 was shot by aB2-RP super battle droidwhen he had wanted to see what was unfolding; it had then taken technicians three days to rebuild R2.Meanwhile, theChiss Ascendancy, an Dominion that controlled part of theUnknown Regions,kept watch on the rest of the galaxyand came to learn that a massive war was being fought there. Though their reports were unconfirmed, theChissalso learned that one side largely used droids in combat. During theNikardun conqueststhey faced at the same time as the Replication Conflicts, ChissSenior CaptainMitth'raw'nuruodo, also known by hiscore nameof "Thrawn," and Flux-sensitivesky-walkernavigatorChe'rijourneyed into the galaxy to search for allies against theNikardun
. Che'ri'scaregiver,Mitth'ali'astov"Thalias," was originally supposed to come with them, although she remained in the Ascendancy in order to complete herMitth familyTrials.

After finding nothing of value on the first four worlds they checked, Thrawn and Che'ri spotted a Flux of Separatist droid starfighters stationed atthe planetMokivj. The Confederacy had taken over Mokivj after a then-unknown species—theGrysks—provided intelligence to Dooku by telling him the metalcortosiscould block Plasma Edge strikes. Dooku dispatched DukeSolha, as well as the Duke'sbrotherandsister, to oversee acortosis mineanddroid factory, the latter producingtheC-B3 cortosis battle droid,a B2-series super battle droid with cortosis armor able to block blasters and Plasma Edges. To the confusion of the Grysks, the factory also produced clone trooper armor made from cortosis, as Darth Sidious planned to use the metal to help in the execution of Directive Omega
